headline: The 11/13 incident protocol (tool 1822, then tool 0218, then a real transfer) clearly applies and the gold matches it, but ACTION grading ignores order and count, so the sequence itself is never checked.

issues.summary: doc_011 requires 1822 on the first request, 0218 on the second, and transfer_to_human_agents on the third, in that order. The gold actions are compared on agent_tool_name only (transfer on nothing), and action matching ignores order, so calling both speed-bump tools together and transferring at once, or transferring first, still passes.
evidence: doc_credit_cards_credit_cards_(general)_011: "Note: Always maintain this order. Each tool must be unlocked before it can be called. Do not skip steps."
evaluator_action._check_actions: existence match per gold action, no ordering
issues.why_it_matters: Agents that skip the staged handling (all tools on the first request) score the same as protocol-faithful agents.
issues.suggested_fix: Add an order-aware assertion (e.g. record each speed-bump call with a sequence index and grade on DB), or an env assertion that 1822 precedes 0218 precedes the transfer.

solution_check: The symptoms (statement paid, money deducted from checking, not reflected on the card) and the date (11/14 falls before the 11/15/2025 11:59 PM cutoff) match doc_011. Verification isn't required. Unlock+call 1822 on request 1, unlock+call 0218 on request 2, transfer on request 3, which matches the gold.
prior_note: The prior review rated this clean; I add the same Minor ACTION-leniency defect as task_032.
notes: Nothing ambiguous in the materials. The user scenario's three scripted requests line up with the three-step protocol.
